1 Angle 01 · Creator haul

Creator haul — “look how much you get”

The reach engine
Revenue50,160
Spend7,302
ROAS6.87
Orders58
CPA126
CTR3.88%

One creator, four tubs, zero on-screen text. It holds attention longer than anything else in the account (18.9% thruplay vs 8–10% for every other video) and absorbs 37% of the budget without breaking — it is the volume driver, not the efficiency winner.

Hook
No text hook. The first frame is the hook: a face + four labelled tubs fanned around it, two dried strawberries held to the cheeks.

Reference recipe

  • Single male creator, chest-up, lived-in living room, natural light.
  • Four different SKUs fanned around his face so the labels read clearly.
  • Hold loose product in both hands (strawberries / mango) — colour contrast on skin.
  • Playful, slightly exaggerated expression in frame 1; smile by frame 2.
  • 0.0s shows product — no logo sting, no title card, no on-screen offer text.
  • Caption + headline carry the offer; the video only sells appetite.

Next variations

  • Swap the creator: female 30s, mother archetype.
  • Swap the SKU set: kids’ favourites (marshmilo, strawberry, mango, pineapple).
  • Same shot, 6 tubs, shot vertically from above — ‘full table’ variation.

A paid creator reel with a failure-first story beats every studio asset: 11.70x ROAS on 3,321 EGP with the cheapest CPA in the account (85 EGP). The hook is a confessed failure, which buys credibility before the product appears.

Hook
جربت اجفف فاكهة بس للاسف كانت النتيجة😔♥️
“I tried drying fruit at home… unfortunately that was the result 😔🤍”

Reference recipe

  • Creator-led reel, native phone quality, no ad polish.
  • Open on the failed DIY attempt (sad face, burnt/collapsed fruit).
  • Hard cut to the Slalah tub already in hand — the rescue moment.
  • One product only; the story carries the range.
  • Creator keeps talking to camera; captions burned in.
  • End on a taste, not a packshot.

Next variations

  • Same script, male creator, gym/snacking context.
  • ‘I tried the oven method’ vs ‘I tried the sun method’ — two hooks, same body.
  • Collab with a food/recipe page instead of a lifestyle creator.

Bundle offer + price anchor (static)

The only static that scales
Revenue39,230
Spend3,561
ROAS11.02
Orders38
CPA94
CTR4.03%
Hookn/a

Angle total includes 3 variants · this ad alone: 3,145 EGP spend, 11.54× ROAS, 35 orders

The basket static posts an 11.54x ROAS and the highest CTR in the account (4.17%). A held basket full of tubs plus an explicit multi-buy offer does the job a video does — it makes the bundle tangible and the maths instant.

Hook
عرض لفترة محدودة! اشتري 4 عبوات واحصل على 2 هدية
“Limited-time offer! Buy 4 tubs, get 2 free.”

Reference recipe

  • Product held in frame — hands and forearms visible, not a floating packshot.
  • Show the actual bundle quantity (4, 5 or 6 tubs) so value is countable.
  • Red ribbon / gift cue on one tub to signal ‘free’.
  • Offer line in Arabic at the top, large, 2 lines max.
  • Brand wordmark small in a corner, never competing with the offer.
  • Price anchoring only where it is honest (bundle price vs crossed-out single-unit total).

Next variations

  • Picky-eaters bundle (kids’ SKUs) with 660 vs 915 anchor.
  • Shella bundle — two large tubs, 995 vs 1,220.
  • 5-box sweet & sour — 1,199 vs 1,700, bright sky-blue background.

Real-world social proof — “it’s out there”

A creator filmed in a retail aisle with the turquoise Slalah bag, jars stacked in front of her. 12.53x ROAS on 1,426 EGP and a 4.39% CTR — the highest of any video. It works because it looks like a stranger’s footage, not an ad.

Hook
No text hook. A public place + a branded bag in hand + phone in the other hand = ‘someone just bought this’.

Reference recipe

  • Shoot in a real retail environment (mall, supermarket, gift shop).
  • Branded bag visible in frame 1, held like a shopping haul.
  • Product tubs lined up in the foreground, labels toward camera.
  • Creator on the phone or mid-reaction — candid, not posed.
  • Native aspect, no captions in the first 2 seconds.
  • Small brand bug top-left only.

Next variations

  • Same idea in a gym, pharmacy or school-run setting.
  • ‘Sold out again’ — empty shelf with one tub left.
  • Customer-style POV: bag on the passenger seat after checkout.

5 Angle 05 · Sensory / ASMR

Sensory / ASMR — hand picking from the platter

Volume filler, cheap attention
Revenue29,119
Spend3,425
ROAS8.50
Orders35
CPA98
CTR3.41%
Hook95.2%
Hold7.8%
Two ad sets running the same video · 41,609 impressions combined

A wooden segmented platter, one hand reaching in, English ‘Buy 2 get 1 free’ overlay. 8.50x on 3,425 EGP across two ad sets — solid, but the weakest CTR of the winners (3.41%) and the lowest hold rate (7.8%): appetite without urgency.

Hook
On-screen English text “Buy 2 get 1 free” over a top-down platter; a hand enters at ~0.5s.

Reference recipe

  • Top-down or 45° shot of a wooden segmented platter with 5–6 SKUs.
  • One hand enters frame and picks a piece — the only motion needed.
  • Text overlay top-centre, 4 words max, high contrast.
  • Muted domestic background (curtains, table) for warmth.
  • No face — keeps cost per asset low for weekly iteration.
  • Pair with offer-led caption; the video alone does not close.

Next variations

  • Kids’ hands instead of adult hands.
  • ASMR crunch audio — record bite close to the mic.
  • Platter + coffee cup for the ‘afternoon snack’ occasion.
03

What the three days actually say

82% / 77%
Video buys attention, statics buy orders
Video took 82% of spend and 77% of revenue; statics took 18% of spend and 23% of revenue. Statics are the more efficient half of the account — the best one is running at 11.5x.
100%
The face is the hook
Every winner puts a human hand or face in frame 1 — no winner opens on a packshot or a logo. The one static that scaled shows hands holding a full basket, not a floating tub.
144 EGP
Packaging does not sell fruit
The unboxing clips spent 144 EGP and returned 0 EGP in tracked revenue. The product has to be edible in frame 1; a pink box is not a reason to buy.

Blindfold taste-test with a creator. 562 EGP for 1,530 EGP back (2.72x) and a 281 EGP CPA — the second-worst video in the set. Fun to watch, weak to buy: the game is the subject, the product is a prop.

Fix to test: Re-shoot so the reaction after the taste is the product benefit, not the joke — or keep it strictly for cold-audience reach at a small, ring-fenced budget.

Method & source

Pulled live from the Meta Marketing API (v21.0) with the store credentials in ~/.claude/creds/stores.json: ad account act_25063361673303941 (“Salalahnuts”), level ad, time_range 2026-11-01 → 2026-11-03, account timezone Africa/Cairo, currency EGP. Revenue and orders are the account’s tracked purchase action values (omni_purchase, falling back to the pixel purchase action); no Shopify-side reconciliation was applied, so returns and cancelled COD orders are not deducted. ROAS = tracked revenue ÷ spend. Hook and Hold are derived from video_play_actions (3s) and video_thruplay_watched_actions. 3 November is a partial day — data was pulled at 17:00 Cairo time, so the final day is under-counted by roughly a third; the ranking held steady at every point during the window.

To share: open this file in a browser and press ⌘P → “Save as PDF” — the layout is print-ready and every image is embedded, so the file works offline as a single artefact.

Creative frames are the ad thumbnails as served by Meta (video thumbnails pulled from the video asset, not from the preview iframe). The collaboration thumbnail was recovered from the Instagram post because the video asset sits on a page the token cannot read.
